contract_completeness: Every required field has an explicit JSON type, shape, defining equation or predicate, and canonicalization rule.

basis_in_generators.canonicalization: row i corresponds to basis i
basis_in_generators.definition: coefficient polynomials representing every basis element

groebner_basis.definition: a lex Groebner basis for the input ideal

leading_monomials.definition: leading exponent vector of each basis polynomial

representation_conventions: Indices are zero-based unless a mathematical exponent or degree is explicitly named. Matrices are row-major; nested tensor array order is stated per task.

A rational scalar is a reduced JSON string "n" or "n/d" with positive denominator. JSON integers are used only where the field contract says integer. Floats, decimal approximations, NaN and infinity are invalid.
The submission object has exactly required_fields, with no additional keys. Nested objects likewise use exactly the named keys.
task_rules: A sparse term is {m:[e_x,e_y,e_z,e_w], c:rational}; exponents are nonnegative, duplicate monomials are forbidden, and canonical term order is descending lex with x>y>z>w.

groebner_basis is an ordered polynomial list. basis_in_generators[i][j] is a coefficient polynomial q_(i,j) such that basis_i=sum_j q_(i,j)*input_generator_j. target_in_generators[j] similarly represents the target.

leading_monomials[i] is the lex-leading exponent of basis_i. Every pair S-polynomial must reduce to zero by ordered first-applicable division by the submitted basis, and the target normal form must be zero.
